why: Same game matched by several roguelike tags; one row per game.

rule: No store details / not a game
why: Delisted or non-game apps have no price, genre or release data.

rule: Release date from store API (search date as fallback)
why: appdetails is the authoritative date; search date only used where the store date is unparseable.
Scope of the study; store date can differ from the search listing used to build the universe.

rule: launch_date = original launch (Early Access start) where earlier than store date
why: Store date is the 1.0 date for games that left Early Access; launch_date is the true launch.

rule: Early Access launch before 2022 (1.0 inside window)
why: Kept per the store-date scope rule; can be excluded in sensitivity checks.

rule: No price (not purchasable in US store at snapshot)
why: Kept: reviews are valid; price-based analyses must exclude or impute these.
Store tag names sometimes carry trailing spaces ('Dystopian ').
Owner estimates unavailable; kept.
Steam totals include hidden/deleted reviews the API no longer returns; per-game coverage is reported.

Largest hits capped to finish the scrape on time and stop them dominating review-level models. Their launch period is missing: exclude from launch/refund-window timing and patch before/after analyses, and use the steam_total_* columns (full Steam totals) for their rating.
Game still in progress when cleaning ran; its reviews are absent from reviews_clean.
Same gid listed twice.
Only the developer's own Steam announcements are used as event dates.
Steam 'patchnotes' tag, or title like patch/hotfix/update/version number, excluding teasers ('coming soon', roadmap), demos, sales, awards and dev blogs.
Developer announcement titled sale/discount/deal/% off; used for price-effect analysis.

rule: Game not in cleaned game table
why: Follows the game-level scope rules above.
A page can be saved twice after a crash/resume, or shift when a new review is posted mid-scrape; the latest edit is kept.
No text to analyse; Steam allows submitting a blank review.
Before 2015 or in the future.
Known Steam API counter bug.
Impossible values.
Score is a probability.

rule: Playtime at review above 99.5% quantile (363 h), capped copy added
why: Steam counts idle/AFK time; raw minutes kept, author_playtime_at_review_capped is the winsorised copy.

rule: Zero or missing playtime at review
why: Pre-release keys, family sharing or playtime not recorded.

rule: Written before launch (incl. Early Access start)
why: Playtests/early keys; kept but can be excluded from launch-timing analyses.

rule: Low content (<3 letters or <2 words; CJK: <4 characters)
why: e.g. 'good', '10/10', '好玩', emoji only: valid votes, little text signal.

rule: ASCII art / symbol spam (>50% symbols, 50+ chars)
why: Meme reviews with no analysable text.
Copied meme/template text or coordinated posting.

rule: Same author, same game, >1 review (info only)
why: Steam allows one review per account per game; non-zero values would point to scrape problems.
Steam's language field is the reviewer's chosen language; topic models are run on English only.
Kept; free copies may bias sentiment, so analyses can control for it.
